body.statement: Using the quotient-enumeration handle, determine whether every distinct tuple in \(\Theta_S(\mathcal O_S)\) can be emitted exactly once, together with a canonical inducing order and positive-definite noise certificate, in total \(O(\operatorname{poly}(p,m)2^p+\operatorname{poly}(p,m)N_{\mathrm{out}})\) exact-real arithmetic operations or with polynomial delay, without visiting every compatible source-to-sink path in \(\mathcal D_S\); if this complexity is impossible in the stated oracle model, derive a matching obstruction.
body.justification: This remains the genuine unresolved step between the compact \(2^p\)-state feasibility DAG and a duplicate-free complete output algorithm; it is not part of the delivered headline kernel.
body.gap: Known enumeration results use graphical signatures, graph-distinct outputs, or a local colored AND--OR congruence. None establishes that global equality of completed modified-Cholesky tuples has the local compositional structure needed here, and the present handle does not define an oracle model supporting a hardness theorem.
body.consumer: A solution would let sparse or degenerate systems emit every distinct full-view coefficient mechanism once even when factorially many compatible orders induce only a few numerical tuples.

obligation.what_is_open: Construct a child oracle that discovers every previously unknown coefficient-tuple fiber exactly once with total additive subset-state and output cost, or first formalize an oracle model and then prove a matching lower bound in that model.
obligation.obstruction: The established fiber lemma canonicalizes inducing orders only after a tuple is known. A removed-set state can be an ideal of many different output support posets, whereas equality of completed coefficient tuples depends on all completed regression rows and is not a frozen local edge color. Testing canonicality separately for every output at every state costs a product of the subset-state and output counts, while traversing all compatible paths can remain factorial even when \(N_{\mathrm{out}}=1\). The present handle supplies neither a polynomial-time inverse-child generator nor a sufficiently formal query model from which an impossibility result could be proved.
obligation.attempted: The prior round examined lexicographically canonical source-to-sink paths, adjacent incomparable swaps, hashing completed paths, locally colored AND--OR quotienting, and reverse search. Lexicographic minimality depends on coefficient rows exposed only by future removals; hashing still visits factorially many paths; local colors have not been shown to form a congruence for global numerical tuples; and reverse search lacks a polynomial-time child oracle for fibers reachable only through noncanonical inducing orders. No hardness assertion is made because the oracle model remains unspecified.
obligation.partial_result: For every \(T\in\Theta_S(\mathcal O_S)\), \(\text{lem:tuple-fiber-linear-extensions}\) proves that its entire compatible inducing-order fiber is the set of linear extensions of \(G_T\). Hence, once \(T\) is known, greedy topological sorting computes its lexicographically least inducing order, adjacent incomparable swaps connect its inducing orders, and \(\Gamma_\pi\succ0\) is computed in time polynomial in \(p\) and \(m\). This removes factorial duplication inside a known fiber, but it does not enumerate previously unknown fibers in \(O(\operatorname{poly}(p,m)2^p+\operatorname{poly}(p,m)N_{\mathrm{out}})\) work or with polynomial delay.
